hero.chip: A camera, a practice diary and a video editor for dancers
hero.title: Watch your {dance grow.}
hero.lead: Film your practice, and your calendar fills with frames of you dancing. Open any day to loop the hard eight-count, slow it down, or set it beside your first try.

how.title: Film. See it on your calendar. {Then really look.}
how.lead: Three steps you'll repeat after every class, rehearsal and practice at home.
steps: Set the tempo, tap record and walk to your mark while it counts you in: 5, 6, 7, 8.
Each take lands on its day as a frame of your own dancing. Several takes stack like prints.
Loop the eight-count you keep missing, slow it to a quarter speed, trim the take, or put it next to your first try.

camera.title: A camera that {knows you're dancing.}
camera.lead: Recording yourself shouldn't mean running back and forth to the phone. Dancify's camera counts you in, keeps you in focus and stays out of the way.
points: Count-in at your tempo
A musical 5, 6, 7, 8 with a click and haptics, so you're on your mark when recording starts.
Follow
Tap a dancer and focus and exposure stay on them as they move. Keep in frame zooms gently to hold them.
Motorised stands
With a DockKit stand, the stand itself turns to follow you across the room.
Every lens
0.5×, 1×, 2×, pinch or the zoom dial. Tap to focus, hold to lock focus and exposure.
Slow motion and 4K
HD or 4K at 30 or 60 fps, and slow motion at 120 or 240 fps for turns and jumps.
Record from across the room
Start with the volume buttons or Camera Control; auto-stop ends the take. Mirror, torch, grid and level are there too.

reference.title: Dance along to {the video you're learning from.}
reference.lead: Play a reference while you film: your own earlier take, a class video, or anything from Photos or Files. Picture-in-picture or side by side, it starts on the count-in's downbeat, so you're together from the first count.
points: Picture-in-picture or side by side
Keep the reference small in a corner, or give it half the screen.
Starts with you on 1
The reference waits for the count-in and starts on the downbeat.
Out of your take
Muted while you film so it stays out of your recording, unless headphones are connected.
Remembered per piece
Each piece keeps its reference and tempo ready for next time.

diary.title: Your practice, {one frame a day.}
diary.lead: Over weeks and months the calendar fills with your own dancing: a visual diary of the work you put in. Log a class without filming, add a note while it's fresh, and find any take again in seconds.
screens: Each day shows a frame from what you danced. Several takes stack like prints. Stage lights or daylight: pick your look.
Every session, take and milestone in order, filtered by takes, sessions or pieces.
Every take of a choreography in order, from first try to full run.

player.title: Drill the hard {eight-count.}
player.lead: Set an A–B loop around the tricky phrase, slow it down, mirror it and count it. The player is made for drilling, not just watching.
points: A–B loop
Mark A and B and it repeats, with an optional eight-count pause between reps to reset.
Counts on screen
1 to 8 in time with the music. Tap the tempo, then jump forward or back by an eight-count.
Slow motion to 0.25×
And frame by frame, to check a landing, a line, or where the arm really goes.
Mirror
Flip the picture to see it the way you'd see it in the studio mirror.
On the big screen
Full screen, AirPlay or an external display, for the whole class to see.
Finds the beat
Dancify listens to a take's music for its tempo and its 1, ready when you turn counts on. Tap your own whenever you like.

editor.title: Edit {like a dancer.}
editor.lead: Trim the take, cut the talking, ramp into slow motion and put the music back. Every edit becomes a new take; your original is never changed.
editor.after: Share it, save it to Photos, or keep it in your diary.
tools: 0.25× to 2×, fine control to 4×, with smooth ramps.
Hold the moment the line is perfect.
Adjustments and looks for studio light.
Captions, a date stamp and a count overlay.
Add a track from Files, with fades in and out.
Mark the moments and change your mind freely.

premium.title: See {how far you've come.}
premium.lead: Day to day, progress is hard to see. Put the first try next to today's and it's obvious.
cards: Two takes played together and lined up to the music, so you see exactly what changed.

Progress reels with the dates on screen, in sequence, side by side or in a grid. Framed for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, or 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9. Dancify saves it to Photos, copies your caption and opens the app.
Lines over your body for shoulders, hips and balance, worked out on your iPhone with Apple's Vision.

privacy.title: Your dancing {stays yours.}
privacy.lead: Practice videos are personal. Dancify keeps them on your device, and in your own iCloud if you want them on all your devices.
items: No account
Open the app and film. No sign-up, no email, no password.
No ads, no tracking
No analytics and no ad networks following you around.
Your own iCloud
Optional sync uses your private iCloud, videos included. We can't see it.
On your device
Follow and the pose guide run on your iPhone. Nothing is uploaded for processing.

styles.title: Whatever you're learning this month.
styles.note: For any routine set to counts or music, from exam pieces to class choreography. It works for floor routines in figure skating and gymnastics too.

faq.title: Questions, {answered.}
items: Is Dancify free?

Yes. Recording, the calendar, timeline, notes, the player, the editor and iCloud sync are free, with no ads and no account. Dancify Premium adds progress reel export, side-by-side compare and the pose guide; it's yearly with a one-week free trial, or monthly.
Which devices does it work on?
iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 26 or later, iPhone Duo included. There's no Android or web version.
Do I need an account?
No. There's no sign-up at all. Your diary lives on your device, and in your own iCloud if you turn sync on.
Where are my videos stored? Can anyone else see them?

Your videos stay on your device. With iCloud sync on, they're also kept in your private iCloud so your other iPhone or iPad can show them. We can't see them, and nothing is uploaded to a server of ours.
How does the count-in work?
Set a tempo, tap record, and Dancify counts you in with a click and haptics, “5, 6, 7, 8”, while you walk to your mark, so you're in place when it starts.
What is Follow?

Tap a dancer in the camera and Dancify keeps focus and exposure on them as they move, holding on if they're briefly hidden. Turn on Keep in frame to zoom gently with them, or use a DockKit motorised stand that turns to follow.
What is Hands-free?

Turn it on in the camera, then raise a hand beside your head, palm open, and hold it still for about a second and a half. The take is saved and the next count-in starts. Standing ready, the same hand starts a take.
Can I practise along to a video?

Yes. Pick a reference, your own earlier take or a video from Photos or Files, and it plays picture-in-picture or side by side while you film, starting with the count-in. It's muted in your recording unless headphones are connected.
Can I slow down and loop one part?
Yes. The player goes down to 0.25× and steps frame by frame. Set an A–B loop around a phrase, with an optional eight-count pause between reps, and turn on counts to see 1 to 8 in time with the music.
Does editing change my original video?
No. Every edit exports as a new take, so the original stays exactly as you filmed it. Share the result or save it to Photos.
Can takes line up to the music?
Yes. When two takes share their music, Compare lines them up on open and keeps them in step, and side-by-side and grid reels start every take on the same moment of the song.
Can I post a reel to TikTok, Instagram or YouTube?

Yes. Reels come in 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, or 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9. Dancify saves the file to Photos, copies your caption and opens the app, so you post it yourself. Progress reel export is part of Dancify Premium.
Which dance styles is it for?
Any style you practise with counts or music: ballet, contemporary, jazz, hip-hop, heels, K-pop covers, salsa and bachata, ballroom, tap, Irish dance, commercial and cheer.
Does Dancify use AI?
No generative AI, and nothing is sent to a server. Follow and the pose guide use Apple's on-device frameworks, so they run entirely on your iPhone or iPad.
Which languages is the app in?
English, German, Finnish, Spanish, French and Japanese.

cta.title: Keep {every practice.}
cta.lead: Free to download. No account, no ads. Film today's practice and it's in your diary.

handsfree.title: Raise a hand. {Go again.}
handsfree.lead: Filming yourself means a lot of walking back to the phone. With Hands-free on, hold a hand up beside your head for a moment, right from your mark.
points: Keep the take and go again
The take is saved and the next count-in starts, so you never leave your mark.
Or start from standing
Ready and in place? The same hand starts the first take.
Saved where it belongs
Each take goes to the piece and kind you filmed last, so the diary stays in order.
Worked out on your iPhone
The camera watches for the hand on the device. Nothing is uploaded.
